provenance: Senses used in sports fandom, transfer rumour culture and match commentary. Football (soccer) transfer Twitter has developed the most codified emoji grammar of any sporting subculture, to the point where single glyphs carry procedural meaning about the status of a deal.

🚨.gloss: In football transfer coverage the siren prefixes a genuine development. Overuse by aggregator accounts has devalued it to the point of parody.

🤝.gloss: The player has agreed with the club; the clubs may not yet have agreed with each other.

✅.gloss: Fabrizio Romano's green tick, signalling a transfer is done. One of the few cases where an individual journalist's habit became an entire community's notation.

✍️.gloss: Completion of paperwork, distinct from agreement in principle.

🩺.gloss: The player is undergoing the medical examination that precedes a signing.

✈️.gloss: Flight tracking is a genuine sub-hobby of transfer season.

🐐.gloss: The central argument-starter of sports discourse; deploying it is a claim, not a description.

🧤.gloss: Position shorthand; also a clean sheet.

🟨.gloss: The plain yellow square is used as a booking marker in live match commentary.

🟥.gloss: Sending off, in the same live-commentary notation.

🔵.sense: deal moving to a specific club
🔵.gloss: Coloured circles stand for club colours in transfer posts; blue commonly Chelsea, Manchester City or Everton depending on the reporter.

🔴.gloss: Typically Liverpool, Manchester United or Arsenal in the same colour-code convention.

⚪.gloss: Los Blancos, in the transfer colour code.

🏆.gloss: Beyond literal trophies, awarded sarcastically to end a debate.

🥇.gloss: Used to assert a hierarchy in list and tier-ranking posts.

🧢.sense: a cap for the national team
🧢.gloss: In football and cricket writing a 'cap' is an international appearance, an older sense entirely unrelated to the slang for lying.

🎽.gloss: The running shirt marks marathon and parkrun posts.

🏋️.gloss: Extended metaphorically to any hard work.

💪.gloss: Support and resolve far more often than literal muscle.

🐍.gloss: The Black Mamba nickname makes the snake a Kobe reference in basketball contexts.

👑.gloss: 'King James'; in NBA discourse the crown is usually a specific person, not generic royalty.

🃏.gloss: 'The Joker'; another player-nickname glyph in NBA fandom.

🦌.gloss: Team-mascot shorthand, typical of NBA emoji conventions.

🎯.gloss: Marksmanship in shooting sports and basketball alike.

📉.gloss: Form collapse, often posted by rival fans.

🪑.gloss: A player not selected; overlaps with the absurdist chair meme.

🏳️.gloss: Rival banter when a scoreline becomes hopeless.

🦅.gloss: Mascot shorthand in NFL and Premier League contexts respectively.

🐓.gloss: The cockerel on the club crest.

🏏.gloss: Often stands for the whole sport in South Asian and Australian social posting.

🥊.gloss: Extended to any public argument or rivalry.

🏃.gloss: Fleeing a conversation rather than athletics.

⛳.gloss: In profile bios, shorthand for a whole social register rather than the sport.
